extracted.intended_audience: readers and scholars of art history; translators and distributors of Project Gutenberg eBooks
extracted.subtask_description: An edition of Giorgio Vasari's Lives (English translation by Gaston du C. De Vere) presented as a Project Gutenberg eBook; the page contains the translator's preface (translation philosophy and editorial choices) and the Project Gutenberg license and distribution requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translator's stated fidelity approach
rubrics_metrics.description: My intention, indeed, has been to render my original word for word, and to err, if at all, in favour of literalness. The very structure of Vasari's sentences has usually been retained...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translator favors literal, word-for-word rendering to preserve Vasari's sense and spirit; expects to reproduce awkwardness of original where necessary; uses punctuation adjustments when needed. Practical implication: prioritize fidelity to original wording and sentence structure over smoothing or paraphrase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of professional/local advice for technical passages
rubrics_metrics.description: In passages full of technicalities, often so loosely used that it is difficult to be sure of their exact meaning, I have invariably adopted the rendering which seemed most in accordance with Vasari's actual words, so far as these could be explained by professional advice and local knowledge; and I have included brief notes where they appeared to be indispensable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For architectural/technical terms, consult subject-matter experts and local sources; where uncertainty remains, choose the rendering most consistent with the original and add brief explanatory notes when indispensable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation and sentence-structure handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The very structure of Vasari's sentences has usually been retained, though some freedom was necessary in the matter of the punctuation, which is generally bewildering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain original sentence structure but adapt punctuation for readability; do not substantially rework sentence flow beyond necessary punctuation changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selective omission of material not directly relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Vasari's Introduction on Technique has not been included, because it has no immediate connection with the Lives. In any case, there already exists an adequate translation by Miss Maclehose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial decision: omit material judged not directly relevant to the edition's focus if adequate translations/sources already exist; document such omissions in preface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lexical choice guidance (example: 'artefice')
rubrics_metrics.description: The word 'artist' has become impossible as a translation of 'artefice.' Such words as 'artificer,' 'art-worker,' or 'artisan,' seem even worse. 'Craftsman' loses the alliterative connection with 'art,' but it comes nearest to expressing Vasari's idea of the 'artefice' as a practical workman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose English equivalents that best capture the original nuance; when common/obvious translations are inadequate, justify the lexical choice in a footnote explaining rationale and alternatives considered.
